questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The language was important, made it easy to connect with the locals. It was very far away and had so much nature that I most likely wouldn't have the chance to see otherwise.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was very easy to get information about all the essentials, either just by looking it up online or asking the school staff.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I used the QUT help desk on campus to find questions about the enrollment process and asked my Airbnb host for questions about the city

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It's very easy to find student accomodations as long as you don't arrive very late for the semester. If you want to find private housing then it's quite difficult, and even using student sharehouse services it is not easy.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Student accomodation is quite expensive but provides clean and secure housing, also makes it way easier to connect with other students and broaden your social circle while you are there. I don't know much about private housing but I had a lot of trouble finding anything and heard it was the same experience for many others. It's worth it if you can find something good, but it a challenge to do that.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I arrived in Brisbane with my pre approved list of courses from UCPH, I then enrolled in 4 of the courses that I wanted the most. After the enrollment had been approved I planned my timetable and then I was set for the semester.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: QUT has a help desk on campus which was very helpful and answered all my questions about the registration process and made it very easy to learn about the school online systems.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the classes I wanted and it was a very smooth process.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Just go to the help desk if you're confused about anything, it helps with all the uncertainty and stress with getting started on the semester.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The courses were in general easier than courses offered on UCPH, where most of the challenges came from managing group work and projects in 4 different courses.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: More practical sessions during the week and a lot more big group assignments, less theoretical in general.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: I took Networks, Advanced Visualization Science, Information Security, and Cryptography.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I would recommend Cryptography if you like more of the theoretical subject, it was interesting and not overbearing with assignments. Advanced Visualization Science was probably my favorite course and I would highly recommend it, a lot of personal freedom in the choice of project you wanna do, and the professor and practicals were very good.
I wouldn't recommend the other two courses, as they were mostly memorization of slides and very stale teaching.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: You have to put down a certain amount of weeks of rent as a bond, which you don't get back until the end of the exchange trip, this was quite a lot of money to have locked away during the trip and should be considered as well (roughly one month of rent as a deposit). Some daily items from the supermarket were also very expensive for danish standarts, but there are really big discounts on some items so i would recommend looking for that.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Public transport was pretty cheap and students can receive 50% if you get a goCard.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Most sports clubs you can think of were there, including surfing and climbing. There were a lot of different cultural clubs for asian countries and quite a few societies, but I didn't really look much into them.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I personally joined the climbing club and it was really nice, they had weekly climbing on an outdoor cliff in the city and in the weekends they would take you on trips to some of the nature/national parks around the city, great way to the bush. The surfclub was also very popular and organized trips to byron bay, also a very good option.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: There is a lot to see around Brisbane, I'll list some of the best day trips that you can do. Lone Pine Koala Sanctuary (must see!), Moreton Island, Stadbroke Island, Gold Coast, Sunshine Coast, Mt Coot-tha. For long trips or holidays you can go to Byron Bay, Noosa Heads and you can also fly pretty easily to Bali, New Zealand or Fiji.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It wasn't too bad since it's mostly just england with a lot more Asian influence. Since everyone spoke english it wasn't really any difficulty adjusting and also plenty of exchange students around if the locals scare you:).

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join clubs, they are super friendly to hang out with and it gives you a way into the daily life of the locals and can give you a lot of insight and ideas as to what you might wanna spend your time with during the semester.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The supermarket is, to no surprise, very different to what we have in Denmark, and it took some time to adjust to that.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Their outgoing nature and outdoor spirit made it easy to make friends and find cool things to do on weekends.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Don't take a first year course, they will be extremely boring. Join clubs and meet some locals, they will give you very valuable information on good places to go and you can also join them for trips sometimes. Lastly, don't book long time accommodation before you arrive, stay in a temporary accommodation for a week or two and have a look around your options in the city, it really helps to see it.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: There are a lot of exchange students from Norway, Germany and also Denmark/Sweden. Just be prepared to meet a lot of familiar people if you join the exchange events.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Seeing the nature and animals, truly amazing landscapes and so many places to go. Meeting people there was also very fun

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: I had 4 roommates and they were very different from me. So getting into clubs and meeting other people through school was really important to me and allowed me to still make great connections with people even if I was unlucky with my roomies.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
